notes: Discovery checklist: Earth regions the PUBLISHED literature names as Moon/Mars analogs, that are NOT in the 16-site catalog and have NO entry in data/campaigns.csv (no NASA/ESA/agency field campaign).

Frozen BEFORE any global-grid result exists. Do not add, remove or move candidates, change expected targets, or change the protocol after seeing grid results. New candidates may be appended later only with a new frozen_on date, reported separately.
Purpose: an independent check that the engine's 'discoveries' are meaningful. A miss is a result too and must be reported, not hidden.
All DOIs verified on Crossref on 2026-11-14.

protocol.requires: data/earth_features.parquet (global grid from the Earth Engine extraction)
protocol.metric: For each candidate: score every land cell (coverage >= 0.5) against the expected target with pure SI (no priority bonuses). Take the best SI among cells within radius_km of the candidate. Report its percentile among all scored land cells.
protocol.chance_level: A random location passes with probability ~10 % (top-10 % threshold); with a radius the best-of-neighbourhood can inflate this, so also report the same statistic for 100 random land points with the same radius as a baseline.
protocol.headline: Report: N of 10 candidates pass (>= 90th percentile) under the science profile, versus the random-point baseline pass rate.

candidates.name: Emi Koussi volcano · Tibesti
candidates.basis: Shield volcano with nested summit calderas used as a close analog of the Martian shield volcano Elysium Mons.

sources.cite: NASA Earth Observatory / JSC Gateway to Astronaut Photography: Emi Koussi Volcano, Chad

candidates.name: Lut Desert megaripples and yardangs
candidates.basis: Large ripple-like aeolian bedforms matching the length scales and patterns of Martian transverse aeolian ridges; mega-yardangs compared with Aeolis yardangs.

sources.cite: Foroutan, M., & Zimbelman, J. R. (2016). Mega-ripples in Iran: A new analog for transverse aeolian ridges on Mars. Icarus.

candidates.name: Wau-an-Namus volcanic field
candidates.basis: First terrestrial site with dark (basaltic) megaripples resembling some Martian transverse aeolian ridges.

sources.cite: Foroutan, M., et al. (2019). Megaripples at Wau-an-Namus, Libya: A new analog for similar features on Mars. Icarus.

candidates.name: Matanumadh jarosite · Kachchh
candidates.basis: Jarosite with gypsum, kaolinite over Fe/Mg smectites in altered Deccan basalts — acid-sulfate alteration analog for early Mars (Gale / Meridiani).

sources.cite: Bhattacharya, S., et al. (2016). Jarosite occurrence in the Deccan Volcanic Province of Kachchh, western India. JGR Planets.

candidates.name: Dhinodhar and Varar volcanic vents · Kachchh
candidates.basis: Basaltic craters and cones proposed as analogs of Ceraunius and Hecates Tholus and Martian volcanic rootless constructs.

sources.cite: Chavan, A., et al. (2022). Volcanic craters and cones in central Kachchh mainland, western India: potential analogues for Mars. Journal of Earth System Science.

candidates.name: Bosumtwi impact crater
candidates.basis: Well-preserved 10.5 km crater holding a lake and lacustrine sediments; ejecta and morphology indicate an originally Mars-like rampart crater.

sources.cite: Baratoux, D., et al. (2019). Bosumtwi impact structure, Ghana: Evidence for fluidized emplacement of the ejecta. Meteoritics & Planetary Science.
Wulf, G., et al. (2019). Earth and Planetary Science Letters: remote sensing + landform evolution modeling of Bosumtwi as a Mars-like rampart crater.

candidates.name: Gilf Kebir · Western Desert
candidates.basis: Core of the largest hyperarid region on Earth: dunes, wind streaks, yardangs and fluvial-aeolian erosion forms compared with Viking images of Mars.

sources.cite: El-Baz, F., et al. (1979). Eolian features in the Western Desert of Egypt and some applications to Mars. JGR.

candidates.name: Central Namib (Gobabeb area)
candidates.basis: Hyper-arid fog desert described as one of the closest Earth analogs to the present Martian surface; lichen colonization studied with rover-style photogrammetry.

sources.cite: Hinchliffe, G., et al. (2017). Frontiers in Microbiology. Advanced photogrammetry to assess lichen colonization in the hyper-arid Namib Desert.

candidates.name: Sittampundi anorthosite complex
candidates.basis: Calcic-plagioclase anorthosite treated as lunar highland rock; source of ISRO's LSS-ISAC-1 highland regolith simulant used to test Chandrayaan-2 landing and mobility.
candidates.prediction_note: Expected to be a mineralogical match but a poor environmental match to the cold lunar pole — a likely MISS under the science profile; included deliberately as a hard case.

sources.cite: Anbazhagan, S., et al. (2011). Remote sensing study of Sittampundi anorthosite complex, India. J. Indian Soc. Remote Sensing.
Anbazhagan, S., et al. (2021). A lunar soil simulant (LSS-ISAC-1) for the lunar exploration programme of ISRO. Icarus.

candidates.name: Jingpo Lake volcanic field
candidates.basis: Holocene effusive volcanic field with pristine cones and lava landforms proposed as a primary terrestrial analog for the lunar Marius Hills.

sources.cite: Yang, et al. (2026). Morphometric analysis of the Jingpo Lake volcanic field: a terrestrial analog for lunar Marius Hills. Remote Sensing.

amendments.reason: Chinese-language search (after the freeze, before any grid result existed) found that Peking University opened a 'lunar-like underground space' teaching and research base in the Jingpo Lake lava tubes in 2025 (data/campaigns.csv id=jingpo_pku). The site is therefore not unstudied. It stays in the checklist (the frozen list is not edited) but is reported separately and excluded from the 'novel' pass count.

batch_2.searched: Chinese- and Russian-language literature and agency news (CNSA/CAS/CUG/PKU, Roscosmos/IBMP/GEOKHI), plus JAXA (Japanese), KASA/KICT, MBRSC and CSA in English.
batch_2.result: No new candidate qualified. Every analog region with a published analog paper in these languages (Qaidam, Jingpo Lake, Leiqiong/Hainan) already hosts a field campaign, so it is not 'unstudied'. Candidates were not forced.

watch_list.note: Plausible regions with NO analog paper found in the searched languages. Not part of the test (no literature basis), but worth inspecting if the global scan ranks them high — that would be a genuine new suggestion, not a rediscovery.

regions.name: Dunhuang yardang field
regions.why: Classic yardangs; Chinese papers study their stratigraphy but none frames them as a Mars analog (Qaidam yardangs are).

regions.name: Lop Nur salt crust
regions.why: Sulfate-bearing salt crust with measured hygroscopic behaviour; no Mars-analog framing found.

regions.name: Wudalianchi volcanic field
regions.why: Young basaltic cones and flows; morphometric studies exist, no direct Mars/Moon comparison found.

regions.name: Tibetan saline lakes (Zabuye, Dangxiong Co)
regions.why: Cold, high-UV borate/lithium evaporite lakes; no Mars-analog study found.

regions.name: Gobi (southern Mongolia)
regions.why: Red iron-oxide desert with large temperature swings; a planned MARS-V tourist habitat (2029) but no analog science paper found.

regions.name: Tolbachik volcanic massif, Kamchatka
regions.why: Popular sources claim Soviet Lunokhod tests here; not verifiable in primary sources, so treated as unconfirmed.
